verdict.rationale: Sentry's source is publicly readable: there is a getsentry/sentry GitHub repository, the docs explain how to run all of Sentry on your own server for free, and a community user describes reading the code to understand its behavior. However, nothing in the pack states which license applies. A community comment in the same thread calls a licensing change 'very disappointing' and describes Sentry as closed-source, which casts doubt on the 'open license' part of the story. Missing for 10: an explicit first-party license statement (e.g., an OSI-approved license), confirmation that the current code is under an open rather than source-available license.
